chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Ya'qub from Marwan ibn Muslim from Ibrahim ibn Muhraz, who said:
A man asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while I was with him. He said: A man said to his wife, 'Your affair is in your hand.' He (the Imam) said: 'How can that be, when Allah the Exalted says,
Men are the protectors/maintainers of women.

key_terms.أَمْرُكِ بِيَدِكِ: Your affair is in your hand (idiom for autonomy)
key_terms.الرِّجَالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ: Men are the maintainers of women (Quranic verse)

ai.seo_question: Is a wife's self-divorce valid if the husband says 'your affair is in your hand'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of 'takhyyir' (delegating divorce authority) by questioning its compatibility with the Quranic principle of 'qawwamun' (men as maintainers). This reflects the Shia scholarly view that while a husband may grant his wife the right to initiate divorce, the ultimate authority and structure remain rooted in the husband's role as the primary maintainer, distinguishing it from a complete transfer of power. The Imam’s rhetorical question underscores that the wife's autonomy is derivative and conditional, not absolute, preserving the hierarchical framework established in Surah An-Nisa.
